summary: Principal Enterprise AI Architect who designed and built Fishbowl's internal agent platform and harness end to end: a sandboxed agent runtime with dispatch, checkpoint/resume, retries, and escalation; a permission-scoped trust boundary so agents never exceed their owner's access; MCP tool federation; provider-agnostic model routing with cost tracking; queryable observability; and an accountable, self-improving memory layer. Shipped to production across chat, Slack, and desktop surfaces. Applied AI Hackathon winner who takes concepts from prototype to production, including MicroFrontend solutions that unify disparate technology stacks.

roles.title: Principal Enterprise AI Architect
responsibilities: Designed and built Atlas, Fishbowl's internal AI agent platform and harness, as principal engineer: an MCP gateway, chat and Slack agent runtime, sandboxed autonomous build engine, and shared agent memory. Delivered in four months across six repositories (1,800+ commits, ~150K lines of TypeScript and Python, 500+ test files, TDD throughout).

Built the agent runtime as a harness-neutral supervisor: a deterministic state machine that drives work through design, implement, review, and fix, calling pluggable coding-harness adapters over a zod-validated step contract that fails closed on malformed model output. Checkpoints after every phase so runs survive pod loss, suspends and escalates to a human on needs_input, and chooses block-in-place versus checkpoint-and-exit based on pool contention.

Owned the trust boundary: every agent run executes in a per-session Kubernetes Job sandbox with egress-locked network policy and short-lived, repo-scoped credentials. An identity broker decides per action whether to act as the user, delegate to a service identity, or deny, with each decision audited. Entra-backed per-user RBAC and per-turn act-as-user JWTs guarantee an agent's ceiling is its owner's permissions, and tool read/write hints drive ask, reads, or all approval tiers.

Shipped the MCP gateway federating ~99 tools across 20+ connectors (Jira, Confluence, Slack, Microsoft 365, GitLab, Salesforce, Gong, Datadog, and more) with a per-user credential vault. The federated connector framework turned the first Salesforce connector into a ~1KB declarative definition, an 87% code reduction covered by 280+ TDD tests, and keeps tools as deterministic primitives while agentic decisions stay above them.

Built the streaming chat runtime on a tool-calling loop with SSE heartbeats to survive proxy idle-cuts, per-result caps to bound context on long tool-heavy turns, and per-thread approvals. Routed all model traffic through a provider-agnostic LiteLLM layer (Claude, GLM, Grok) with dedicated routes so extraction, memory, and embedding spend is accounted separately, and designed an advisor-model pattern with per-run cost and timing telemetry to measure marginal dollars per avoided human intervention.

Built Hermes, a resident agent-quality supervisor on a generic workflow-event bus, with a shared fleet memory (FastAPI, mem0, pgvector). Memories carry candidate and durable tiers, TTL horizons, a single redaction chokepoint, and fail-open 150 ms recall. A five-layer background pass re-scores each memory on whether the runs that recalled it succeeded, with corroboration-gated promotion, per-source reliability discounting, confidence ceilings, tombstoned audit records, and human-reviewed proposals for destructive changes (running on dev).

Made every agent action queryable: a versioned canonical telemetry envelope with trace-id propagation and tiered redaction, append-only audit, and Datadog integration. Added an automated failure-triage agent that investigates failed runs in a read-only sandbox and produces a root-cause report with a copy-paste fix prompt, plus an LLM-judge chat quality eval that scores turns without ever persisting raw text.

Extended the platform across surfaces and agents: Themis, an orchestrator that decides intent with a model but executes only through RBAC-gated primitives; a Tauri desktop and browser Studio built on single-spa micro-frontends with a swappable chat transport; integration of the Pi coding agent into the same sandbox; and versioned agent profiles baked into harness images.
